assessments.reasoning: Bytes [5348,5851) identify the license as the instrument suffering partial failure, preserve its remainder and apply the purpose limit to both branches of the undertaking. The earlier waiver-failure language has a different trigger and consequence. Neither passage binds another rightsholder to the Affirmer's undertaking.

challenge.method: Test waiver failure with a fully effective fallback, then partial failure of the fallback itself. In the latter case, test whether the undertaking also bars an exercise of rights consistent with the stated purpose.
challenge.results: Waiver failure alone triggers the fallback grant. Partial failure of the license triggers the residual undertaking. The introduction describes a purpose of allowing the public to reuse and adapt the Work without fear of later infringement claims. Conduct consistent with that purpose falls outside the undertaking's prohibition, although other terms may still govern it.

limitations: Enforceability, the consistency of specific conduct with the stated purpose, and the outcome of any dispute require separate evidence.
reasoning: The closing condition in section 3 specifically addresses a judgment about part of the fallback license. That failure leaves the rest of the license intact. The purpose qualification governs both exercising remaining rights in the Work and asserting associated claims or causes of action.
